ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE SCHOOL MEALS ACT

Article 1 (Purpose) 
The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe the matters delegated by the School Meals Act and the Enforcement Decree of the same Act, and those necessary for the enforcement thereof.

Article 2 (Report, etc. on Commencement of School Meal Services) (1) The report on the commencement of school meal services pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the School Meals Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Decree") shall be made in accordance with the written report on commencement of school meal services according to the format of Form 1 by no later than ten days prior to the commencement of meal services.
  (2) For the report on the change pursuant to Article 3 (2) of the Decree, the contents thereof shall be reported within 20 days from such change.
  (3) The head of a school shall report the current status of the meal services as of the end of each school year to the Minister of Education (hereinafter referred to as the "Minister") or the Superintendent of the Office of Education (hereinafter referred to as the "Superintendent") in accordance with the current status of implementation of meal services according to the format of Form 2 by Feb. 28, and the Superintendent shall report thereof to the Minister by Mar. 20. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (4) The Minister or the Superintendent shall enter the matters reported pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (3) into the educational information system referred to in Article 30-4 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, and manage them. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 3 (Detailed Standards for Meal Service Facilities) (1) The detailed standards for the facilities and their appurtenant facilities referred to in Article 7 (2) of the Decree shall be as stated in the attached Table 1.
  (2) The specific standards such as the capacities of the refrigerating and freezing facilities, and equipment, machine and tools related with cooking and meal services, among the standards pursuant to paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by the Superintendent.

Article 4 (Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals) (1) The standards for quality control of food materials pursuant to Article 10 (2) of the School Meals Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") shall be as stated in the attached Table 2.
  (2) In the event that quality shall be preferentially taken into account to elevate the quality of school meals and to secure the safety thereof, the contracts for purchasing food materials may utilize the methods of entering contracts by negotiation, pursuant to Article 43 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which the State is a Party or Article 43 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government is a Party.

Article 5 (Standards for Nutrition Control of School Meals) (1) The standards for nutrition control of school meals pursuant to Article 11 (2) of the Act shall be as stated in the attached Table 3.
  (2) The matters to be taken into consideration at the time of preparation of menus in accordance with paragraph (1) shall be as follows:
  1. Succession and development of traditional dietary culture shall be considered;
  2. Various kinds of foodstuffs such as grains, starches, vegetables and fruits, fish, meat and beans, milk and dairy products shall be used;
  3. Salt, oils and fats, simple sugars or food additives shall not be overused;
  4. Natural foodstuffs and seasonal foodstuffs shall be used if possible; and
  5. A variety of cooking methods shall be utilized.

Article 6 (Standards for Sanitation and Safety Control of School Meals) (1) The standards for sanitation and safety control of school meals pursuant to Article 12 (2) of the Act shall be as stated in the attached Table 4.
  (2) The Minister may determine the guidelines for observance and improvement of the standards pursuant to paragraph (1). <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 7 (Observance Matters for Quality and Safety) (1) The term "other matters necessary for the quality and safety of school meals" in Article 16 (2) 2 of the Act refers to the following matters: <Amended on Nov. 22, 2013>
  1. Disclosure of the percentage of expenses for foodstuffs among the expenses for meals borne by the guardians for each semester; and
  2. Keeping and storing of documents related with school meals (storage period shall be three years):
    (a) Journal of school meals stating number of persons served with school meals, menus, quantity of nutrition supplies, etc.; and
    (b) Journal of inspection of food materials and itemized accounts of transactions.
  (2) Where the head of a school, school meal service teaching and other staff under the head, or a school meal service provider uses in school meals any food subject to allergenic-substance labeling under Article 5 (1) and Appendix 2 of the Enforcement Rule of the Act on Labeling and Advertising of Foods, they shall give notice and display that information by the following methods pursuant to Article 16 (3) of the Act. However, for a food containing an ingredient obtained from such food by extraction or another method, they may follow the methods below. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 22, 2013; Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>
  1. Method of giving notice: A monthly menu indicating food materials that may cause allergies shall be provided through a notice sent to homes and posted on the school's website.
  2. Method of display: A weekly menu indicating food materials that may cause allergies shall be posted in the dining room and classrooms.

Article 8 (Visit, Inspection, etc.) (1) Entry, inspections, etc. of facilities under subparagraph 1 of Article 14 of the Decree shall be conducted as follows; however, the Minister or the Superintendent may adjust the annual frequency where deemed necessary. <Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>
  1. Confirmation on whether or not of fulfilling the standards for quality control of food materials pursuant to Article 4 (1), standards for nutrition control pursuant to Article 5 (1), and the observance matters pursuant to Article 7 and guidance thereof shall be implemented not less than once a year, and it may be simultaneously implemented at the time of confirmation and guidance of subparagraph 2; and
  2. Confirmation on whether or not of fulfilling the standards for sanitation and safety pursuant to Article 6 (1) and guidance thereof shall be implemented not less than twice a year.
  (2) Where deemed necessary for efficient entry, inspections, etc. of facilities under subparagraph 2 of Article 14 of the Decree, the Minister, the Superintendent, or the head of the relevant district office of education may request administrative assistance from the Minister of Food and Drug Safety, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do governor, a Special Self-Governing Province governor, or the head of a Si, Gun, or Gu (referring to the head of an autonomous Gu). <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013; Nov. 22, 2013>
  (3) The public official concerned who has conducted the visit and inspection pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2) shall record the results thereof in the journal of visits and inspections according the format of Form 3 kept in the facilities related with the relevant school meal services.
  (4) The identification card indicating the authority of public officials pursuant to Article 19 (2) of the Act shall be in accordance with the format of Form 4.

Article 9 (Collection and Request, etc. for Inspection) (1) The following inspection may be conducted pursuant to Article 19 (1) of the Act:
  1. Testing for microorganisms and
  2. Inspection of the place of origin, quality and safety of food materials.
  (2) The public official who has collected the material to be inspected shall seal such material at the place of collection, and have it stamped or signed by the relevant public official and the collected person, and without delay request the inspection agency concerned such as the public health and environment research institute in the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan City, Do, or Special Self-Governing Do, or the public health clinic of the city/Gun/Gu for the inspection, or directly conduct the inspection: Provided, that for the inspection under paragraph (1) 2, he/she may request the administrative agency concerned such as the National Agricultural Products Quality Management Service, the Animal and Plant Quarantine Agency, or the National Fishery Products Quality Management Service for collection and inspection thereof. <Amended on Nov. 22, 2013>
  (3) In the event of collecting the material to be inspected pursuant to paragraph (2), he/she shall deliver the certificate of collection according to the format of Form 5; and when he/she has requested for inspection, he/she shall record the contents thereof in the register of disposition on collection and inspection according to the format of Form 6, and shall keep it.

Article 10 (Request, etc. for Administrative Disposition) 
In the event of intending to request the head of the competent administrative agency for necessary dispositions such as administrative dispositions, etc. pursuant to Article 21 of the Act, such request shall be filed by attaching the confirmation letter according to the format of Form 7 or the result of inspection under Article 9 (1).

Article 11 (Review of regulations)
The Minister of Education shall examine the validity of the detailed standards for meal service facilities under Article 3 and Appendix 1 every two years, taking January 1, 2015 as the reference date (meaning before the day corresponding to that reference date in each second year), and shall take measures for improvement, etc.

Detailed Standards for Meal Service Facilities (Related to Article 3 (1))
■ Enforcement Rule of the School Meals Act [Appendix 1] <Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>

Detailed Standards for Meal Service Facilities (Related to Article 3 (1))
1. Kitchen
(a) Facilities and equipment
1) The kitchen shall be located in sanitary and pleasant surroundings, without a risk of flooding and with protection from sources of contamination such as dust; noise, odors, etc. from the kitchen shall not interfere with students' learning.
2) To prevent cross-contamination during work, the kitchen shall be divided by walls and doors into areas such as a preliminary preparation room, cooking room, and dishwashing room, separating the general work area from the clean work area. However, where such partitioning is inappropriate, other measures to prevent cross-contamination shall be taken.
3) The kitchen shall have an adequate area for work and maintenance of cleanliness, taking into account the arrangement of meal service equipment and utensils and the movement of workers.
4) Interior walls shall be made of durable, water-resistant materials with smooth surfaces.
5) The floor shall be made of durable, water-resistant materials and shall not be slippery.
6) The ceiling shall be made of water-resistant and fire-resistant materials that are easy to clean.
7) Drainage outlets of an adequate size and covers shall be installed at appropriate positions in the floor in a manner facilitating cleaning.
8) Entrances and windows shall have appropriate equipment, such as insect screens, to prevent the entry of insects and rats.
9) Shoe-disinfection equipment shall be provided at the entrance to the kitchen.
10) Ventilation equipment shall be installed to rapidly discharge steam, unpleasant odors, etc. from the kitchen.
11) Kitchen lighting shall be at least 220 lux (lx). However, the inspection area shall have lighting of at least 540 lux (lx).
12) Handwashing facilities shall be installed at necessary locations in the kitchen.
13) To control temperature and humidity, the kitchen shall be equipped with air supply and exhaust equipment, heating and cooling equipment, or air-conditioning equipment, etc. of an appropriate capacity.
(b) Equipment and utensils
1) Cooking appliances, such as rice cookers, soup kettles, and gas ranges, shall be selected from products without risks such as fire or explosion; efficient appliances shall be installed, considering material safety and the durability and economy of the appliances.
2) Refrigerators (refrigerated rooms) and freezers shall maintain capacities and temperatures sufficient for storing food materials, thawing frozen food materials, cooling foods that have been cooked by heating, etc. (refrigerators: 5°C or lower; freezers: -18°C or lower).
3) To perform cooking, serving, and other work hygienically, food-washing facilities, cooking facilities, dishwashing facilities, utensil storage cabinets, covered waste containers, etc. shall be provided. Parts in contact with food shall be made of water-resistant and corrosion-resistant materials that are easy to wash and capable of being disinfected and sterilized.
4) Dishwashers shall have automatic washing and rinsing functions.
5) For disinfection of tableware and utensils, an electric sterilizer, an ultraviolet disinfector, or a hot-water disinfection facility shall be provided, or a washing sink capable of adequate washing and disinfection shall be installed.
6) Hot-water supply equipment shall be provided so that meal service utensils, serving tools, etc. can be washed safely and hygienically.
2. Food storage rooms, etc.
(a) A food storage room and a supplies storage room shall be installed separately. However, where it is not possible to install them separately for unavoidable reasons, they shall be separated by partitioning the space or by other means.
(b) The floor material shall be easy to wash with water, nonslip, and well drained.
(c) Ventilation equipment, sufficient storage shelving, etc. shall be installed; the shelving shall have a structure facilitating cleaning and air circulation.
3. Meal service management room and amenities
(a) The meal service management room and rest room shall be accessible from outside without passing through the cooking room, and shall have ventilation equipment leading outside. However, where the structure makes an external entrance difficult to install, necessary measures shall be taken to prevent contamination of the cooking room during entry and exit.
(b) The rest room shall have wardrobes permitting outdoor clothing and sanitary work clothing to be stored separately, so that outdoor clothing does not contaminate sanitary work clothing.
(c) Where a shower room is installed, ventilation equipment leading outside shall be provided to prevent contamination of the cooking room.
4. Dining room: A dining room of a size appropriate to the number of persons served shall be provided so that meals can be eaten in a safe and sanitary space. However, a school that has difficulty providing a separate dining room, including because of insufficient space, shall have transport equipment and hygienic serving tools necessary for serving meals in classrooms.
5. Matters not prescribed in these standards shall follow the facility standards for institutional food service under food sanitation statutes and regulations.

Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals (Related to Article 4 (1))
Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals (Related to Article 4 (1))
1. Agricultural products
(a) Agricultural products labeled with their place of origin under Article 5 of the Act on Origin Labeling of Agricultural and Fishery Products and Article 33 of the Foreign Trade Act shall be used. However, this shall not apply to agricultural products that are not food materials subject to origin labeling.
(b) Products falling under any of the following categories shall be used.
1) Organic foods, etc. and pesticide-free agricultural products certified under Articles 19 and 34 of the Act on the Promotion of Environment-Friendly Agriculture and Fisheries and the Management of and Support for Organic Foods, Etc.
2) Among standard products under Article 5 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act, agricultural products graded "high" or better under the agricultural product standards. However, where no standard has been established for an agricultural product, products with a commercial value corresponding to "high" or better shall be used.
3) Agricultural products certified for good agricultural practices under Article 6 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
4) Agricultural products subject to traceability management under Article 24 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
5) Agricultural products with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
(c) Rice within one year of its harvest year shall be used.
(d) Where it is unavoidable to use preprocessed agricultural products (food materials processed after harvest into a form immediately usable in cooking through washing, sorting, peeling, cutting, etc.), products meeting items (b) and (c) and displaying the following information shall be used.
1) Product name (name or category of the contents).
2) Business name (name of the producer or producer organization).
3) Date of manufacture (date of preprocessing and date of packaging).
4) Quality of the food material before preprocessing (place of origin, quality grade, and year of production).
5) Net quantity.
6) Storage and handling instructions.
(e) Imported agricultural products shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in items (b) through (d).
2. Livestock products
(a) The common standards are as follows. However, these common standards shall not apply to edible eggs under Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
1) Meat processed at a slaughterhouse applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 (2) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act shall be used.
2) Livestock products processed at a livestock product processing plant or meat packaging plant designated as a workplace applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 (3) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act shall be used. The same shall apply where imported livestock products are processed or packaged in Korea.
(b) The individual standards are as follows. However, for chicken, eggs, and duck, they shall constitute recommendations until the grading system is fully implemented.
1) Beef: Korean native cattle beef and beef cattle meat graded 3 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
2) Pork: Pork graded 2 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
3) Chicken: Chicken graded 1 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
4) Eggs: Eggs graded 2 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
5) Duck: Duck graded 1 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
6) Imported livestock products: Products complying with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act, Food Sanitation Act, and Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act, and having a quality equivalent to that prescribed in 1) through 5) shall be used.
3. Fishery products
(a) Fishery products labeled with their place of origin under Article 5 of the Act on Origin Labeling of Agricultural and Fishery Products and Article 33 of the Foreign Trade Act shall be used.
(b) Quality-certified products under Article 14 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act, fishery products with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of that Act, or products with a commercial value corresponding to "high" or better shall be used.
(c) Preprocessed fishery products
1) Where preprocessed fishery products (food materials processed into a form immediately usable in cooking through washing, sorting, cutting, etc.; hereinafter the same shall apply) are used, they shall meet item (b) and shall have been processed at one of the following facilities or businesses. The same shall apply where imported fishery products are processed in Korea.
(a) Production or processing facilities registered with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as facilities implementing hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 74 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
(b) Food manufacturing or processing businesses handling fish or mollusk products among frozen fishery foods under Article 62 (1) 2 of the Enforcement Rule of the Food Sanitation Act, as businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
2) Where preprocessed fishery products are used, they shall display the following information.
(a) Product name (name or category of the contents).
(b) Business name (name of the producer or producer organization).
(c) Date of manufacture (date of preprocessing and date of packaging).
(d) Quality of the food material before preprocessing (place of origin, quality grade, and year of production).
(e) Net quantity.
(f) Storage and handling instructions.
(d) Imported fishery products shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in items (b) and (c).
4. Processed foods and other items
(a) Products falling under any of the following categories shall be used.
1) Traditional foods quality-certified under Article 22 of the Food Industry Promotion Act.
2) Processed agricultural, livestock, or fishery products certified as conforming to industrial standards under Article 15 of the Industrial Standardization Act.
3) Foods with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
4) Quality-certified products under Article 14 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
5) Processed foods produced at businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
6) Processed foods produced at food manufacturing or processing businesses registered under Article 37 of the Food Sanitation Act.
7) Processed livestock products processed or treated at businesses applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
8) Processed livestock products displaying the manufacturer, expiration date, etc. in accordance with labeling standards under Article 6 (1) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
(b) Finished kimchi products shall be products produced at businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
(c) Imported processed foods shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in item (a).
(d) Foods and food additives not specified above shall comply with food sanitation statutes and regulations.
5. Exceptions
(a) Where the supply of food is disrupted by flooding, drought, natural disasters, etc., the quality control standards need not be applied.
(b) For food materials not prescribed in this table, or where applying the standards for quality control of food materials for school meals is considered difficult because the school is in an island or remote area, is small, or because of local conditions, the Superintendent may establish and implement separate quality control standards following deliberation by the school meal services committee.

(c) In principle, vitamin A, thiamin, riboflavin, vitamin C, calcium, and iron shall be supplied in amounts not less than the recommended intakes under the standards for nutrition control of school meals, and shall at least meet the average requirements.

Standards for Sanitation and Safety Control of School Meals (Related to Article 6 (1))
■ Enforcement Rule of the School Meals Act [Appendix 4] <Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>

Standards for Sanitation and Safety Control of School Meals (Related to Article 6 (1))
1. Facility management
(a) Plans for cleaning and disinfecting meal service facilities, equipment, utensils, etc. shall be established and implemented to keep them clean at all times.
(b) The temperatures of refrigerators and freezers, the final rinse-water temperature of dishwashers, or the temperature of tableware disinfection and storage cabinets shall be recorded and managed.
(c) Where groundwater, rather than tap water, is used for meal services, it shall be disinfected or sterilized before use.
2. Personal hygiene
(a) Food handlers and cooking workers shall undergo a health examination once every six months, and the records shall be retained for two years. However, examination for pulmonary tuberculosis may be conducted once a year.
(b) Hands shall be washed thoroughly to prevent contamination through the hands. However, hand disinfection may be performed where necessary.
3. Food material management
(a) Menus shall be planned considering whether foods are potentially hazardous, and processing operations shall be strictly controlled.
(b) When food materials are inspected upon receipt, their quality, freshness, quantity, sanitary condition, etc. shall be checked and recorded to ensure conformity with the Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals.
4. Work hygiene
(a) Cooking utensils and containers, such as knives, cutting boards, and rubber gloves, shall be used separately according to purpose and shall be washed and disinfected frequently to prevent cross-contamination from raw materials or during cooking.
(b) Food handling and other work shall be performed at a height of at least 60 cm above the floor to prevent food contamination.
(c) Cooked foods and washed and disinfected serving utensils and containers shall be managed so that they are not contaminated by contact with utensils, containers, raw materials, etc. posing a risk of cross-contamination.
(d) Thawing shall be carried out under refrigeration (10°C or lower), in a microwave oven, or in running water (21°C or lower).
(e) Thawed food shall be used immediately.
(f) Vegetables and fruits eaten raw shall be thoroughly washed and disinfected.
(g) For foods cooked by heating, a thermometer shall be used to check that their centers are heated to at least 75°C (85°C for shellfish) for at least one minute, and the temperatures shall be recorded and maintained.
(h) The temperature and time of cooked foods shall be managed to suppress microbial growth and toxin production.
5. Serving and food checks
(a) For safe meal services, transport and serving utensils, etc. for cooked food shall be kept clean, and measures shall be taken to prevent contamination by such utensils during serving.
(b) Where food is transported to and served at a place outside the meal service room, transport equipment and vehicles, etc. shall be kept clean so that the food is not contaminated before serving.
(c) Immediately before serving cooked food, checks shall be conducted to verify its taste, temperature, harmony (nutritional balance and balance of ingredients), foreign matter, unpleasant odors, degree of cooking, etc.
(d) Where food cooked in meal service facilities is not subject to temperature control, serving shall be completed within two hours after cooking.
(e) For each meal service, one serving of cooked food shall be retained at -18°C or lower for at least 144 hours.
6. Washing and disinfection, etc.
(a) After washing and disinfection, tableware and utensils shall be stored and managed hygienically until serving.
(b) Meal service facilities shall be disinfected under Article 24 of the Enforcement Decree of the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act, and certificates of disinfection shall be kept on site.
7. Safety management
(a) Periodic safety inspections under the relevant provisions shall be conducted, including gas, fire, and electrical safety inspections and inspections of boilers, pressure vessels, and dumbwaiters.
(b) To prevent accidents involving cooking machines and utensils, safe operating procedures shall be posted, training shall be provided, a person responsible for management shall be designated and indicated by a label, and thorough management shall be ensured.
(c) Kitchen floors shall be kept nonslip to prevent accidents.
8. Other matters: Matters not prescribed in these standards shall follow the sanitation and safety standards under food sanitation statutes and regulations.

Article 2 (Report, etc. on Commencement of School Meal Services) (1) The report on the commencement of school meal services pursuant to Article 3 (1) of the Enforcement Decree of the School Meals Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Decree") shall be made in accordance with the written report on commencement of school meal services according to the format of Form 1 by no later than ten days prior to the commencement of meal services.
  (2) For the report on the change pursuant to Article 3 (2) of the Decree, the contents thereof shall be reported within 20 days from such change.
  (3) The head of a school shall report the current status of the meal services as of the end of each school year to the Minister of Education (hereinafter referred to as the "Minister") or the Superintendent of the Office of Education (hereinafter referred to as the "Superintendent") in accordance with the current status of implementation of meal services according to the format of Form 2 by Feb. 28, and the Superintendent shall report thereof to the Minister by Mar. 20. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>
  (4) The Minister or the Superintendent shall enter the matters reported pursuant to paragraphs (1) through (3) into the educational information system referred to in Article 30-4 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, and manage them. <Amended on Mar. 4, 2008; Mar. 23, 2013>

Detailed Standards for Meal Service Facilities (Related to Article 3 (1))
■ Enforcement Rule of the School Meals Act [Appendix 1] <Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>

Detailed Standards for Meal Service Facilities (Related to Article 3 (1))
1. Kitchen
(a) Facilities and equipment
1) The kitchen shall be located in sanitary and pleasant surroundings, without a risk of flooding and with protection from sources of contamination such as dust; noise, odors, etc. from the kitchen shall not interfere with students' learning.
2) To prevent cross-contamination during work, the kitchen shall be divided by walls and doors into areas such as a preliminary preparation room, cooking room, and dishwashing room, separating the general work area from the clean work area. However, where such partitioning is inappropriate, other measures to prevent cross-contamination shall be taken.
3) The kitchen shall have an adequate area for work and maintenance of cleanliness, taking into account the arrangement of meal service equipment and utensils and the movement of workers.
4) Interior walls shall be made of durable, water-resistant materials with smooth surfaces.
5) The floor shall be made of durable, water-resistant materials and shall not be slippery.
6) The ceiling shall be made of water-resistant and fire-resistant materials that are easy to clean.
7) Drainage outlets of an adequate size and covers shall be installed at appropriate positions in the floor in a manner facilitating cleaning.
8) Entrances and windows shall have appropriate equipment, such as insect screens, to prevent the entry of insects and rats.
9) Shoe-disinfection equipment shall be provided at the entrance to the kitchen.
10) Ventilation equipment shall be installed to rapidly discharge steam, unpleasant odors, etc. from the kitchen.
11) Kitchen lighting shall be at least 220 lux (lx). However, the inspection area shall have lighting of at least 540 lux (lx).
12) Handwashing facilities shall be installed at necessary locations in the kitchen.
13) To control temperature and humidity, the kitchen shall be equipped with air supply and exhaust equipment, heating and cooling equipment, or air-conditioning equipment, etc. of an appropriate capacity.
(b) Equipment and utensils
1) Cooking appliances, such as rice cookers, soup kettles, and gas ranges, shall be selected from products without risks such as fire or explosion; efficient appliances shall be installed, considering material safety and the durability and economy of the appliances.
2) Refrigerators (refrigerated rooms) and freezers shall maintain capacities and temperatures sufficient for storing food materials, thawing frozen food materials, cooling foods that have been cooked by heating, etc. (refrigerators: 5°C or lower; freezers: -18°C or lower).
3) To perform cooking, serving, and other work hygienically, food-washing facilities, cooking facilities, dishwashing facilities, utensil storage cabinets, covered waste containers, etc. shall be provided. Parts in contact with food shall be made of water-resistant and corrosion-resistant materials that are easy to wash and capable of being disinfected and sterilized.
4) Dishwashers shall have automatic washing and rinsing functions.
5) For disinfection of tableware and utensils, an electric sterilizer, an ultraviolet disinfector, or a hot-water disinfection facility shall be provided, or a washing sink capable of adequate washing and disinfection shall be installed.
6) Hot-water supply equipment shall be provided so that meal service utensils, serving tools, etc. can be washed safely and hygienically.
2. Food storage rooms, etc.
(a) A food storage room and a supplies storage room shall be installed separately. However, where it is not possible to install them separately for unavoidable reasons, they shall be separated by partitioning the space or by other means.
(b) The floor material shall be easy to wash with water, nonslip, and well drained.
(c) Ventilation equipment, sufficient storage shelving, etc. shall be installed; the shelving shall have a structure facilitating cleaning and air circulation.
3. Meal service management room and amenities
(a) The meal service management room and rest room shall be accessible from outside without passing through the cooking room, and shall have ventilation equipment leading outside. However, where the structure makes an external entrance difficult to install, necessary measures shall be taken to prevent contamination of the cooking room during entry and exit.
(b) The rest room shall have wardrobes permitting outdoor clothing and sanitary work clothing to be stored separately, so that outdoor clothing does not contaminate sanitary work clothing.
(c) Where a shower room is installed, ventilation equipment leading outside shall be provided to prevent contamination of the cooking room.
4. Dining room: A dining room of a size appropriate to the number of persons served shall be provided so that meals can be eaten in a safe and sanitary space. However, a school that has difficulty providing a separate dining room, including because of insufficient space, shall have transport equipment and hygienic serving tools necessary for serving meals in classrooms.
5. Matters not prescribed in these standards shall follow the facility standards for institutional food service under food sanitation statutes and regulations.

Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals (Related to Article 4 (1))
Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals (Related to Article 4 (1))
1. Agricultural products
(a) Agricultural products labeled with their place of origin under Article 5 of the Act on Origin Labeling of Agricultural and Fishery Products and Article 33 of the Foreign Trade Act shall be used. However, this shall not apply to agricultural products that are not food materials subject to origin labeling.
(b) Products falling under any of the following categories shall be used.
1) Organic foods, etc. and pesticide-free agricultural products certified under Articles 19 and 34 of the Act on the Promotion of Environment-Friendly Agriculture and Fisheries and the Management of and Support for Organic Foods, Etc.
2) Among standard products under Article 5 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act, agricultural products graded "high" or better under the agricultural product standards. However, where no standard has been established for an agricultural product, products with a commercial value corresponding to "high" or better shall be used.
3) Agricultural products certified for good agricultural practices under Article 6 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
4) Agricultural products subject to traceability management under Article 24 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
5) Agricultural products with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
(c) Rice within one year of its harvest year shall be used.
(d) Where it is unavoidable to use preprocessed agricultural products (food materials processed after harvest into a form immediately usable in cooking through washing, sorting, peeling, cutting, etc.), products meeting items (b) and (c) and displaying the following information shall be used.
1) Product name (name or category of the contents).
2) Business name (name of the producer or producer organization).
3) Date of manufacture (date of preprocessing and date of packaging).
4) Quality of the food material before preprocessing (place of origin, quality grade, and year of production).
5) Net quantity.
6) Storage and handling instructions.
(e) Imported agricultural products shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in items (b) through (d).
2. Livestock products
(a) The common standards are as follows. However, these common standards shall not apply to edible eggs under Article 2, subparagraph 6 of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
1) Meat processed at a slaughterhouse applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 (2) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act shall be used.
2) Livestock products processed at a livestock product processing plant or meat packaging plant designated as a workplace applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 (3) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act shall be used. The same shall apply where imported livestock products are processed or packaged in Korea.
(b) The individual standards are as follows. However, for chicken, eggs, and duck, they shall constitute recommendations until the grading system is fully implemented.
1) Beef: Korean native cattle beef and beef cattle meat graded 3 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
2) Pork: Pork graded 2 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
3) Chicken: Chicken graded 1 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
4) Eggs: Eggs graded 2 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
5) Duck: Duck graded 1 or better under Article 35 of the Livestock Industry Act shall be used.
6) Imported livestock products: Products complying with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act, Food Sanitation Act, and Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act, and having a quality equivalent to that prescribed in 1) through 5) shall be used.
3. Fishery products
(a) Fishery products labeled with their place of origin under Article 5 of the Act on Origin Labeling of Agricultural and Fishery Products and Article 33 of the Foreign Trade Act shall be used.
(b) Quality-certified products under Article 14 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act, fishery products with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of that Act, or products with a commercial value corresponding to "high" or better shall be used.
(c) Preprocessed fishery products
1) Where preprocessed fishery products (food materials processed into a form immediately usable in cooking through washing, sorting, cutting, etc.; hereinafter the same shall apply) are used, they shall meet item (b) and shall have been processed at one of the following facilities or businesses. The same shall apply where imported fishery products are processed in Korea.
(a) Production or processing facilities registered with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as facilities implementing hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 74 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
(b) Food manufacturing or processing businesses handling fish or mollusk products among frozen fishery foods under Article 62 (1) 2 of the Enforcement Rule of the Food Sanitation Act, as businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
2) Where preprocessed fishery products are used, they shall display the following information.
(a) Product name (name or category of the contents).
(b) Business name (name of the producer or producer organization).
(c) Date of manufacture (date of preprocessing and date of packaging).
(d) Quality of the food material before preprocessing (place of origin, quality grade, and year of production).
(e) Net quantity.
(f) Storage and handling instructions.
(d) Imported fishery products shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in items (b) and (c).
4. Processed foods and other items
(a) Products falling under any of the following categories shall be used.
1) Traditional foods quality-certified under Article 22 of the Food Industry Promotion Act.
2) Processed agricultural, livestock, or fishery products certified as conforming to industrial standards under Article 15 of the Industrial Standardization Act.
3) Foods with registered geographical indications under Article 32 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
4) Quality-certified products under Article 14 of the Agricultural and Fishery Products Quality Control Act.
5) Processed foods produced at businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
6) Processed foods produced at food manufacturing or processing businesses registered under Article 37 of the Food Sanitation Act.
7) Processed livestock products processed or treated at businesses applying hazard analysis and critical control point standards under Article 9 of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
8) Processed livestock products displaying the manufacturer, expiration date, etc. in accordance with labeling standards under Article 6 (1) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.
(b) Finished kimchi products shall be products produced at businesses applying food safety management certification standards under Article 48 (1) of the Food Sanitation Act.
(c) Imported processed foods shall comply with relevant statutes and regulations, including the Foreign Trade Act and Food Sanitation Act, and shall have a quality equivalent to that prescribed in item (a).
(d) Foods and food additives not specified above shall comply with food sanitation statutes and regulations.
5. Exceptions
(a) Where the supply of food is disrupted by flooding, drought, natural disasters, etc., the quality control standards need not be applied.
(b) For food materials not prescribed in this table, or where applying the standards for quality control of food materials for school meals is considered difficult because the school is in an island or remote area, is small, or because of local conditions, the Superintendent may establish and implement separate quality control standards following deliberation by the school meal services committee.

Standards for Sanitation and Safety Control of School Meals (Related to Article 6 (1))
■ Enforcement Rule of the School Meals Act [Appendix 4] <Amended on Jan. 29, 2021>

Standards for Sanitation and Safety Control of School Meals (Related to Article 6 (1))
1. Facility management
(a) Plans for cleaning and disinfecting meal service facilities, equipment, utensils, etc. shall be established and implemented to keep them clean at all times.
(b) The temperatures of refrigerators and freezers, the final rinse-water temperature of dishwashers, or the temperature of tableware disinfection and storage cabinets shall be recorded and managed.
(c) Where groundwater, rather than tap water, is used for meal services, it shall be disinfected or sterilized before use.
2. Personal hygiene
(a) Food handlers and cooking workers shall undergo a health examination once every six months, and the records shall be retained for two years. However, examination for pulmonary tuberculosis may be conducted once a year.
(b) Hands shall be washed thoroughly to prevent contamination through the hands. However, hand disinfection may be performed where necessary.
3. Food material management
(a) Menus shall be planned considering whether foods are potentially hazardous, and processing operations shall be strictly controlled.
(b) When food materials are inspected upon receipt, their quality, freshness, quantity, sanitary condition, etc. shall be checked and recorded to ensure conformity with the Standards for Quality Control of Food Materials for School Meals.
4. Work hygiene
(a) Cooking utensils and containers, such as knives, cutting boards, and rubber gloves, shall be used separately according to purpose and shall be washed and disinfected frequently to prevent cross-contamination from raw materials or during cooking.
(b) Food handling and other work shall be performed at a height of at least 60 cm above the floor to prevent food contamination.
(c) Cooked foods and washed and disinfected serving utensils and containers shall be managed so that they are not contaminated by contact with utensils, containers, raw materials, etc. posing a risk of cross-contamination.
(d) Thawing shall be carried out under refrigeration (10°C or lower), in a microwave oven, or in running water (21°C or lower).
(e) Thawed food shall be used immediately.
(f) Vegetables and fruits eaten raw shall be thoroughly washed and disinfected.
(g) For foods cooked by heating, a thermometer shall be used to check that their centers are heated to at least 75°C (85°C for shellfish) for at least one minute, and the temperatures shall be recorded and maintained.
(h) The temperature and time of cooked foods shall be managed to suppress microbial growth and toxin production.
5. Serving and food checks
(a) For safe meal services, transport and serving utensils, etc. for cooked food shall be kept clean, and measures shall be taken to prevent contamination by such utensils during serving.
(b) Where food is transported to and served at a place outside the meal service room, transport equipment and vehicles, etc. shall be kept clean so that the food is not contaminated before serving.
(c) Immediately before serving cooked food, checks shall be conducted to verify its taste, temperature, harmony (nutritional balance and balance of ingredients), foreign matter, unpleasant odors, degree of cooking, etc.
(d) Where food cooked in meal service facilities is not subject to temperature control, serving shall be completed within two hours after cooking.
(e) For each meal service, one serving of cooked food shall be retained at -18°C or lower for at least 144 hours.
6. Washing and disinfection, etc.
(a) After washing and disinfection, tableware and utensils shall be stored and managed hygienically until serving.
(b) Meal service facilities shall be disinfected under Article 24 of the Enforcement Decree of the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act, and certificates of disinfection shall be kept on site.
7. Safety management
(a) Periodic safety inspections under the relevant provisions shall be conducted, including gas, fire, and electrical safety inspections and inspections of boilers, pressure vessels, and dumbwaiters.
(b) To prevent accidents involving cooking machines and utensils, safe operating procedures shall be posted, training shall be provided, a person responsible for management shall be designated and indicated by a label, and thorough management shall be ensured.
(c) Kitchen floors shall be kept nonslip to prevent accidents.
8. Other matters: Matters not prescribed in these standards shall follow the sanitation and safety standards under food sanitation statutes and regulations.
